implementation_notes: scala.concurrent supplies the fan-out directly: Future.traverse(recipients)(r => r.deliver(copy)) schedules one future per recipient on the ExecutionContext and yields a Future of the collected results, failing with the first delivery error. Continue-on-error is expressed by making each element a Future[Try[Result]] before traversing, so per-recipient outcomes survive into the result. Akka/Pekko Streams (Source(recipients).mapAsync) or a broker client add back-pressure and durability, but the runtime list plus traverse already is the pattern - no router component is needed.
pitfalls: Blocking sends on the global ExecutionContext starve its ForkJoinPool; wrap them in blocking { } or hand them a dedicated fixed thread pool.
Future.traverse fails fast while the remaining futures keep running, so 'the fan-out failed' never means 'nothing was delivered' - partial delivery is the norm.
Sharing one mutable message instance across the traversed futures races; each delivery needs its own copy.
